newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Feb indust output growth seen quickening.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Feb indust output growth seen quickening.

text.p: Rising exports should help boost Slovak February industral output, but analysts said on Monday there was little chance of reaching growth levels of a year ago.
The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) is expected to release figures for February industrial output on Tuesday. No exact time has been set for the release of the data.
Analysts said February production should grow by 3-5 percent, year-on-year, compared with a 2.0 percent rise in January, but well down from February 1996 when year-on-year growth was 9.6 percent.

"I think output can grow faster than it did in January, somewhere between three to four percent year-on-year, mainly due to faster growing exports in the first two months of the year," said ING Barings an analyst Martin Barto.
Barto added output should continue to grow over the year given the expected economic growth of Slovakia's main trading partners.

"Longer-term growth will depend on developments in target export countries but output may continue growing throughout the year driven by expected economic growth by a strong trading partner such as Germany," he said.

Last month SUSR said Slovakia's exports totalled 45.373 billion crowns in the first two months of this year, an increase of 13.1 percent over January-February 1996. In January exports rose only 0.9 percent year-on-year.
Germany alone accounted for 26 percent of Slovakia's exports, followed by Austria and Italy, with 6.1 and 5.4 percent, respectively.
Milan Duroch, analyst at Tatra Banka, also said he expects rising exports to drive industrial output higher, forecasting a growth of up to five percent for February.

"Import demand in reviving western economies can help increase our export production and boost industrial output, which we foresee at up to five percent year-on-year in February," Duroch told Reuters.
But Charlie Robertson of the London-based independent economic think-tank HILFE warned against too big hopes that German economic growth would solve chronic export problems.

"We have cut down our full-year forecast for industrial production growth to 2-4 percent, from 3-5 percent, year-on-year mainly due to remaining problems of export efficiency in the Slovak economy," he said.

"When you look at the end of the last year German growth was mostly export-led and I doubt there'll be too much room on the German market for Slovakia's exports this year. At least certainly not in the first half of the year."
